lead: Cleveland plumbing deals with lake-effect cold, old housing, basements and lead service lines. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Cleveland.
risk: lead and galvanized service lines, basement backups and frozen pipes
risk_short: lead lines, basement backups and frozen pipes
why: Cleveland has a large share of homes built before 1940, especially in Ohio City, Tremont, Detroit-Shoreway and Slavic Village. Many have galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines.
Heavy storms overload older sewers and push water back into basements. Lake-effect cold freezes pipes in exterior walls and vacant homes.
water: Cleveland Water draws from Lake Erie through intakes far offshore. The water is moderately hard. Many older homes still have lead service lines, and the utility has information on replacing them.
tips: Ask Cleveland Water about your service line material.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: PipeMend works in Ohio City, Tremont, Detroit-Shoreway, University Circle, Old Brooklyn, Slavic Village and every other Cleveland neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Cleveland Department of Building and Housing. Ohio licenses commercial plumbing contractors. The city sets the rules for home plumbing work.

faq.q: Does my Cleveland home have a lead water line?
faq.a: It might. Many homes built before the 1950s have lead service lines. Cleveland Water has an address lookup, and a plumber can check the pipe where it enters your basement.
